sam (support): Customer on a Dedicated pool reporting short bursts of 429s after a quota update yesterday. low steady QPS but intermittent throttles. @mia can you triage?

mia (eng-runtime): on it — any repro steps or curl they ran? :eyes:

sam (support): they sent this minimal repro, 3 quick calls and third gets 429:
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-dedicated-16\",\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset-in: 600
x-rate-limit-scope: tenant:acme
```

jon (eng-sre): can you paste the tenant quota config (redacted) and recent quota-sync logs? my gut says denom mismatch (minutes vs hours) or defaulting.

sam (support): redacted tenant config snippet they shared:
```json
{"tenant_id":"acme","rate_units":"per_minute","burst":120,"sustained":7200,"cooldown_seconds":3600}
```

mia (eng-runtime): whoa — sustained=7200 + per_minute looks off. If interpreted as hours -> much lower effective qps. Check quota-sync logs for unit_denominator handling.

sam (support): quota-bot log excerpt from yesterday's sync:
```
WARN quota-sync: unit_denominator missing for tenant acme, defaulting to hours
INFO quota-sync: applied sustained=7200 (denom=hours) -> mapped_rate=2 rps (approx)
```

jon (eng-sre): that's the issue. UI/billing shows per_minute but sync defaulted to hours and runtime used mapped_rate -> small sustained rate. During autoscaler warmup or small burst, tokens consumed faster -> 429s.

mia (eng-runtime): mitigation options: 1) temporary tenant override increase burst/sustained 2) re-run quota-sync with explicit denom set to minutes 3) hotfix quota-sync to error on missing denom. I'll apply a temporary override and push a guard.

sam (support): can you repro locally so we can attach repro to ticket?

mia (eng-runtime): yes — run this sim:
```bash
./tools/run-tenant-sim --tenant acme --qps 5 --duration 300
```
Expect 429s after warmup when mapping is wrong.

jon (eng-sre): root-cause summary for incident notes: quota-sync defaulted unit_denominator to hours when plan migration omitted explicit denom; mismatch between admin UI (per_minute) and sync mapping caused effective quota to be much smaller than intended. Combined with dedicated pool warmup/autoscaler behavior -> transient windows where requests exceeded per-tenant limit producing 429s.

sam (support): customer asked for ETA on permanent fix and wants temporary mitigation now.

mia (eng-runtime): applying tenant override now (bump burst x10) and re-running sync with explicit denom. will open PR for hotfix to quota-sync to fail loudly on missing denom and add test coverage.

sam (support): applied override + re-sync confirmed. ACME reports sharp drop in 429s within 10m. :thumbsup:

quota-bot: created ticket RWD-2026-512: quota-sync-denom-missing-fails-safely

ops-bot: autoscale events during incident window: 2026-03-12T22:15Z scale 4->8 GPUs, 22:18Z stable at 8, 22:40Z scale-down to 5.

jon (eng-sre): follow-ups: (1) enforce explicit denom on plan migrations, (2) add alert when quota-sync applies defaulted denom, (3) instrument runtime to log if mapped_rate << UI rate for the tenant.

mia (eng-runtime): opening PR with tests + repro steps + runbook entries. will link to RWD-2026-512.

sam (support): thanks — I'll message customer with mitigation steps and ETA for permanent fix. closing when PR merged and alerting in prod removed.

sam (support): marking as resolved for now, will reopen if ACME sees regression.
